section.title: Workflow Discovery
section.purpose: Select the smallest high-value workflow and specify it end-to-end.

questions.title: Workflow candidates
questions.prompt: Which repeated workflows consume the most time, money, attention or opportunity?

questions.title: Workflow #1
questions.prompt: Which single workflow should be automated or augmented first?
questions.recommendation: Choose the strongest economic wedge, not the coolest demo.

questions.title: Workflow #2
questions.prompt: What is the second workflow if #1 succeeds?
questions.recommendation: Do not build it until #1 passes proof.

questions.title: Trigger
questions.recommendation: A workflow without a deterministic start is underspecified.

questions.title: Required context
questions.prompt: What information must exist before Workflow #1 may act?
questions.recommendation: List data, documents, state, permissions and history.

questions.title: Current steps
questions.prompt: What are the actual current steps from trigger to completion?
questions.recommendation: Observe where possible; do not rely only on ideal SOPs.

questions.title: Decision branches
questions.prompt: Which decisions or branches change the path?
questions.recommendation: Capture if/then logic and decision owner.

questions.title: Exceptions
questions.prompt: Which unusual cases break the normal process?

questions.title: Tools touched
questions.prompt: Which systems must Workflow #1 read or write?

questions.title: Completion output
questions.prompt: What artifact, state change, message or completed task marks the end?

questions.title: Frequency / volume
questions.prompt: How often does the workflow run and what is peak volume?

questions.title: Current cost
questions.prompt: How much human time, delay, error or opportunity does it consume now?

questions.title: Failure modes
questions.prompt: What can go wrong and what is the consequence of each failure?

questions.title: Workflow rollback
questions.prompt: How can each action/write be reversed or recovered?
